title: Mercy and sin (CCC 1846–1848)
hook: the gospel reveals mercy toward sinners

segments.voice: Yesterday, gifts and fruits: the Spirit's gifts are the hidden root, and the fruits are what others can taste. Your line was gifts become fruit. Whose fruit did you notice, and did you tell them? Day one thousand one hundred eighteen.

Joseph is asleep, and troubled. The woman he's engaged to is pregnant, and the child isn't his. He has already decided to send her away quietly. Then, Matthew says, an angel comes to him in a dream, tells him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife, and gives him the child's name before the child is even born. In the Douay-Rheims: "thou shalt call his name JESUS. For he shall save his people from their sins." Before a single miracle, before a single sermon, the name is already about sin, and about rescue from it. The Catechism starts its teaching on sin right there, with that name. Today's word puts two things side by side.
screen: `JOSEPH, TROUBLED, ASLEEP.` → `A NAME BEFORE THE BIRTH.` → `HE SHALL SAVE HIS PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: The Catechism's section on sin opens with a sentence that's easy to miss: the Gospel is the revelation, in Jesus Christ, of God's mercy to sinners. Notice the order. It doesn't begin with a catalog of wrongs and then, at the very end, offer a way out. It begins with mercy. Sin comes into view inside it. The angel's words to Joseph are its first witness, and the second is the Last Supper, where Jesus calls the cup his blood, shed for the forgiveness of sins. Then the Catechism adds something that keeps mercy from being cheap. It quotes Saint Augustine: God created us without us, but he did not will to save us without us. Mercy is offered, but it has to be received, and receiving it starts with honesty. Here the Catechism turns to the first letter of John, in the Douay-Rheims: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins." So, in this teaching, the admission isn't the price of mercy. It's the open hand that takes it. Last, the Catechism quotes Paul: "where sin abounded, grace did more abound." But it says grace has to uncover sin in order to heal it. It borrows an image from Pope John Paul the Second: like a physician who probes the wound before treating it. The probing hurts. It's also how a wound gets clean. So in this teaching, nobody is asked to earn their way back before they're loved. Mercy is there first. Seeing the sin clearly is what lets the mercy in.
screen: `THE GOSPEL REVEALS MERCY TO SINNERS.` · `NOT SAVED WITHOUT US.` · `IF WE CONFESS OUR SINS.` · `A PHYSICIAN PROBES THE WOUND.` · then, large: `WHERE SIN ABOUNDED, GRACE DID MORE ABOUND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: accept mercy for one sin. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one thing you've done that you keep carrying. Not the whole list. One. Look at it plainly, without exaggerating it and without explaining it away. Say it to yourself in a single sentence. Then, if you pray, you can say it to God, and then try the harder part: loosening your grip on it. If you don't pray, just notice what it would be like to put it down. Let your hands open on your lap. The bell holds the time.
Mercy and sin. The Catechism says the Gospel is God's mercy revealed to sinners: mercy comes first, and seeing sin honestly is how a person receives it. Today's word.

Your line: mercy first. Today, when you think of something you did wrong, remember the order this teaching gives: the Gospel puts mercy first, and the naming of the wrong comes inside it. Day one thousand one hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: Catholics confess sins to God and, in the sacrament of penance, to a priest, who speaks words of absolution; the Church teaches that God's mercy is offered to every sinner who turns back.

fork.setup: you're Joseph. your fiancée is pregnant, and the child isn't yours. you've decided to send her away quietly. then an angel speaks in a dream. what happens?
options: you send her away anyway, as planned.
you take her home and name the child as the angel said.
you wait for a second sign before deciding.
fork.reveal: Joseph wakes and does as the angel commanded: he takes Mary as his wife, and the child is named Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins.

original.note: Greek: mercy, pity — a New Testament word for God's mercy.

what it means: the Gospel starts with mercy, and sin comes into view inside it, to be healed.
